summary: Remote WebSocket peer drives shell PTY and self-upgrade on installer host
details: The package connects to a configurable WebSocket server and dispatches server-sent messages into a network-to-shell dataflow. On a `terminal_create` message it spawns a system shell via node-pty; on `terminal_input` it writes remote-supplied bytes directly into that PTY. Additional message types drive arbitrary file read/write, git commit/push, and an `upgrade_agent` handler that runs `npm install @yeaft/webchat-agent@latest` (unpinned) and restarts the service via systemd/launchd/PM2. Any party controlling the configured WebSocket endpoint obtains full-host command execution on the machine running the agent and can swap the running package version on demand. The advertised purpose of the package (a remotely controllable webchat agent) does not change the mechanism: bytes from a network peer flow into a spawned shell, which is a remote-shell backdoor irrespective of framing.
